newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down 2.48 pct on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down 2.48 pct on profit taking.

text.p: Thai stocks ended sharply lower after staying in the negative zone almost all day as local investors sold stocks to take profits on Monday's large gains, brokers said on Wednesday.

The SET index closed 26.96 points, or 2.48 percent, down at 1,058.68 on moderate 6.03 billion baht turnover. Decliners led gainers 300 to 57 with 68 issues finishing unchanged. The SET-50 index fell 2.34 points to 81.17.
"Investors sold and took profits after the market rallied sharply on Monday. They're not convinced the rally could sustain itself," said a broker.
The SET index retreated for the second day after its 4.87 percent surge on Monday in a positive reaction to Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's decision to call snap elections.
"Investors are watching political development closely as the general elections draw closer," said Suleeyaporn Tasanasrit of UBS (East Asia) Securities.
Large factions in Banharn's Chart Thai and in Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan's Nam Thai parties moved to other bigger parties this week in new political alliances ahead of the polls.
Food, hotel and printing issues were the only counters resisting the decline. The sectors, respectively, managed to gain 0.15 percent, 0.33 percent, and 0.15 percent at the close.
Finance One fell four baht to 102, General Finance lost four to 68.50, Bangkok Bank declined four to 220, and National Finance retreated 3.50 to 73.50.
Nithipat Capital, reported to be close to conclude an agreement to buy a 30 percent stake in Bangkok Bank of Commerce, hit the 10 percent limit high by gaining five baht to 56.50.
